text:
The Penguins had gone four games without a win, and Arturs Silovs ended that run by stopping all 26 Florida shots in a 4-0 shutout at PPG Paints Arena. He saved about two and a half goals more than the quality of those shots should have allowed (that is what goals saved above expected measures), and the best look Florida had, an 18 percent chance from Sam Reinhart in the third period, never got past him.

The game itself was closer than the score. Florida had 52 shot attempts to Pittsburgh's 43 and led in expected goals, which add up the quality of every chance, 2.29 to 3.22 only because of a late Penguins surge. Through two periods Florida had the edge in the second, 1.07 to 0.78. Based on the chances created, the Panthers deserved to win 56 percent of the time, meaning they came out ahead in 56 percent of simulated replays of every shot. Pittsburgh scored on chances that were not especially good: Nick Robertson's opener in the first period came on an 18 percent look, Hendrix Lapierre's goal in the second on a 24 percent one, and Evgeni Malkin's early in the third on just 13 percent. Neither team scored on the power play, with Florida 0 for 4 and Pittsburgh 0 for 3.

Robertson sealed it with his second of the night late in the third, a wrist shot that left it 4-0. Florida's Cooper Black stopped 17 of 20 and allowed about one goal more than expected. The Penguins end their winless stretch, while the Panthers take a shutout loss, one in which they outplayed their opponents for long stretches and had nothing to show for it.
